coaching.headline: Six fights won and one cashed: the towers, not the kills, decided this loss.
coaching.team: The draft ran 4 of 5 damage magical against an enemy built 3 of 5 physical around Greystone, who closed with 42,657 damage to heroes, while the roster carried just one anti-heal item against Lt. Belica's healing and no armor at all on the offlane. Laning split unevenly: the carry lane against Skylar and the jungle read against Khaimera both favored us, the offlane against Greystone ran even, and both the midlane against Gideon and the support lane against Lt. Belica played from behind the entire game. The team still out-fought the opponent in raw kills, 27 to 18, and won six of the fights that mattered to the opponent's four, but conversion told the real story: only one of those six wins turned into an objective, while the opponent turned all four of theirs. River control went the same way across the match, 7 river camps to their 18 and 0 seedlings taken to their 3, and two of the biggest majors, the Mini Prime at minute 18 and the Fangtooth at minute 22, went to the opponent with the entire roster alive and nobody sent to stop them. Towers finished 1 to 13. The fight at 31.2, lost 0-2 near the enemy's Primal Fangtooth, triggered the final collapse: the carry, ahead in lane, and the offlane, alive but never joining, both stayed out of it, and Renna's death there fed the Primal Fangtooth and, across the next minute, two inhibitors and the core. The focus for the next game is straightforward: group before contesting the next major instead of splitting across the map, and turn a lane lead into a rotation rather than continued farm.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The swing point sat between minute 18 and minute 22: the Mini Prime fell uncontested with the entire roster alive, and the Fangtooth followed the same way even though the team won the fight for it 4-1 — the objective still went to the opponent. From there, converting a fight mattered more than winning one: across the match the roster won six fights but converted only one into an objective, while the opponent converted all four it won.
coaching.whatWorked: The clearest strength was the pick fight at the team's own Fangtooth at 7.9: Phase and GRIM.exe caught three of the five enemy heroes there and won it 3-0, and that fight converted straight into the Fangtooth secured at minute 8.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31's Phase carried the vision game, placing 13 wards, the most on the roster, and died only once across the match while picking up 12 assists — the map presence and peel a support gets graded on were both there. The lane against Lt. Belica was lost the entire game, though, and that shows up directly in the macro read: Phase was marked alive but pinned in a losing lane during the fight at 18.3, lost 0-2 outside the enemy Mini Prime, and again during the fight at 25.3, lost 0-2 outside their Inner Tower, both flagged as the wrong fight to start with that lane state.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324's GRIM.exe led the roster in damage to heroes, 39,871, and kills, 9, winning the carry lane against Skylar outright for the entire game. The build skipped two of the three community core items, Lightning Hawk and Dust Devil, replacing them with four off-meta picks built around ultimate haste and damage: Necrosis, Nuclear Rounds, Overseer and Spear Of Desolation. The lane lead carried the numbers anyway, but it never turned into fight participation: GRIM.exe was marked alive and ahead in lane yet absent from the fight at 18.3 outside the enemy Mini Prime and the fight at 31.2 outside their Primal Fangtooth, both losses that a shove-and-rotate could have flipped. The 25.4 death also fed directly into the Orb Prime and two inhibitors that fell soon after.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's Countess ran even with Greystone in lane and took no deaths before minute 16, giving the frontline job a clean start. The build never carried an armor item, though, against a comp that was 3 of 5 physical with Greystone alone hitting for 42,657 damage to heroes. Countess was also marked alive and never joining two of the fights that decided the game: the fight at 25.3, lost 0-2 outside the enemy Inner Tower, and the fight at 31.2, lost 0-2 outside their Primal Fangtooth; getting that body to either fight changes the count.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's Zarus held a favored jungle read against Khaimera on paper, but Khaimera drew first blood on him alone at minute 3, and the tempo never came back: 8 deaths, the most on the roster, and only 3 completed items by the end. The build also passed on Tainted Blade, the one core piece that carries anti-heal, for Citadel's armor-shred instead — against a Khaimera whose kit leans entirely on healing off the damage he deals, that gap let his sustain through.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs' Renna produced the roster's second-leading number of picks behind GRIM.exe's 9, with 8 kills, and the second-most damage, 35,029, in a midlane matchup against Gideon that was lost the entire game. Four of Renna's five deaths each fed a tower or objective within 90 seconds, from the outer tower that fell at 14 through the Primal Fangtooth, two inhibitors and the core that all fell in the final minute of the game after the 31.2 death.

22.call: The fight at 22, won 4-1 against a four-man engage, still cost the Fangtooth: while the roster fought and killed four of the five enemy heroes, nobody was sent to stop the objective, and it went to the opponent uncontested in the same window. Winning bodies doesn't secure the buff on its own; the better call is peeling a body toward the objective the moment a fight like that is clearly won.

7.9.call: Grouping two into a pick fight worked because it caught three of the five enemy heroes without the rest of their team: Phase and GRIM.exe won it 3-0 next to the team's own Fangtooth, and that pressure paid straight into the Fangtooth secured at minute 8. That's the shape worth repeating: fight where the win pays into an objective already up.

31.2.call: The fight at 31.2, lost 0-2 outside the enemy's Primal Fangtooth, was only 2 of ours against 2 of theirs while the carry, ahead in lane, and the offlane, alive but never rotating in, both stayed out of it. A full group there wins that fight and holds the objective; instead the death fed the Primal Fangtooth and, over the next minute, two inhibitors and the core.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Phase's build hit the full three-item community core: Marshal for the on-hit poke and 15% attack speed, Enra's Blessing for the shield an ally gets the instant they're locked down, and Galaxy Greaves for physical-and-magical armor plus mana regen. The extra two slots went to Windcaller, which speeds up Phase and a healed ally after a heal or shield, and Vanguardian, an aura that hands nearby allies 15 physical and 12 magical armor. Against a Lt. Belica the team faced with only one anti-heal item all game, none of Phase's five items answer healing directly, leaning the kit fully into shields and armor instead of cutting the enemy's own sustain.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: The engine's pick for Phase is Vesh, whose major turns ability hits into a stacking damage-over-time effect that grows the longer the game runs, a fit for a link-enchanter whose passive already heals off her own ability casts and whose kit favors the longer fight. That trades away a single burst-window major for damage that adds up over repeated casts, which suits a support who spent the game pinned in a lost lane against Lt. Belica rather than initiating fights herself. This is theoretical: the match feed does not record which Eternal was actually equipped.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: GRIM.exe's build kept only Plasma Blade of the three community core pieces, skipping Lightning Hawk's attack-speed-and-crit base with its empowered-basic slow, and Dust Devil's stacking attack speed and movement speed. In their place came four items built around the ultimate instead: Necrosis and Overseer each push GTFO's damage up by 15%, Spear Of Desolation adds ultimate haste plus a 10% damage window after casting it, and Nuclear Rounds scales ability damage off crit chance. The swap traded the on-hit carry identity for an ultimate-focused one, and it still produced the team's highest damage to heroes, 39,871, so the alternate route paid off in output even without the core.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: The engine's pick for GRIM.exe is Demiurge, rewarding a finished six-item build with 12% more stats from items and 10% more item-effect damage, and GRIM.exe did finish all five items bought this game, tied with Phase for the fullest build on the roster. That scaling major trades away an early-game burst option, but it lines up with the ultimate-stacking route the actual build took and with a carry who won the lane against Skylar outright. It is theoretical; the feed doesn't record the Eternal actually run.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Countess's build matched two of the three community core pieces, the Orb line for magic power and health that scales with level, and Noxia for the mark-and-detonate proc, but missed the third, Lifebinder, which trades magic power for lifesteal that grows the more health Countess is missing — a natural fit for a fragile assassin leaning on prolonged trades. The fourth slot went to Tainted Scepter, for the 45% anti-heal on magic damage, and Overseer, for 15% more ultimate damage, rather than that sustain piece. The bigger gap sat outside the core entirely: the build never carried an armor item at all, against a comp that was 3 of 5 physical with Greystone alone hitting for 42,657 damage to heroes.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: The engine's pick for Countess is Demiurge, the same item-scaling major run across half this roster, rewarding a completed six-item build over any single burst window. Countess closed with only 4 completed items, so that late payoff wasn't fully reached, and the trade costs a burst-focused major that would have punched up the Feast-suppress combo the kit is actually built around. It's theoretical, since the feed doesn't show which Eternal was equipped, but the fit reads better on paper than it played out in this loss.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Zarus's build kept Berserker's Axe, for the leap-empowered basic, and Augmentation, for the on-hit burst after casting an ability, two of the three community core pieces. The third, Tainted Blade, never went in; it carries the team's only other source of the 45% anti-heal that the kit notes call mandatory against Khaimera's health-regen passive. Citadel took that slot instead, shredding 20% physical armor off nearby enemies — useful pressure, but it does nothing to cut the sustain that let Khaimera keep dueling through the damage Zarus put on him.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: The engine's pick for Zarus is Krix, a health-stacking major that also grants bonus size, paired with Festering Wounds, a second grievous-wound source that would have helped cover the same anti-heal gap the item build left open against Khaimera. It fits the trap-and-out-duel win condition by turning Zarus into a harder target to kill outright, though the major needs levels and completed health items to anchor a fight, and Zarus finished only 3 items after getting caught for first blood at minute 3. This loadout is theoretical, since the match feed doesn't record which Eternal was actually run.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Renna's build hit the full three-item community core: Entropy for repeated bonus magic damage on ability hits, Wraith Leggings for a flat 12% amp to all ability damage, and Overseer for 15% more ultimate damage. The fourth slot added Megacosm, which burns a chunk of a target's max health over time on ability hits, a pick built for chewing through the enemy's tankier frontline, Greystone included. The core itself wasn't the issue this game; Renna only finished 4 of a planned six items, so even a build that matched the community's preferred path didn't get to run its full course before the game ended.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: The engine's pick for Renna is Demiurge, the third hero on this roster running the same item-scaling major, rewarding a finished six-item build with more stats and stronger item effects. That fits a zone mage whose win condition is chunking a grouped fight from range once fully built, but it is a slow-burn major for a lane that was lost against Gideon all game and a build that stalled at 4 completed items. It's theoretical, since the feed doesn't record which Eternal actually ran, but the trade-off between early safety and late scaling reads as a mismatch with how far behind the midlane fell.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Lt. Belica. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 magical — predictable; one magic-resist item answers most of it. Mix in a physical threat.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
